title: Human periodontal ligament–bone interface model with a root-facing attachment
question: Can a staged human-cell construct achieve a viable ligament compartment with oriented collagen insertion at both a root-facing mineral interface and a bone-facing interface, while avoiding mineral bridging and retaining recoverable mechanical response?
claim_boundary: This is an in-vitro model design. It cannot establish tooth repositioning, intact-socket trauma repair, durable human attachment, rejuvenation, or clinical benefit.
experimental_unit: Independent human donor/cell preparation and manufacturing batch; constructs, sections, image fields, and repeated loads are nested observations.

published_chassis.contribution: PDLSC-laden collagen printed on excised root fragments; in-vitro migration and alignment; ectopic root-fragment implantation in immunocompromised mice through 4 and 10 weeks.
published_chassis.transfer_limit: No alveolar socket or physiological tooth load; the authors describe parallel alignment as short of functional fiber insertion, and the in-vitro root-surface experiment did not observe new cementum.

published_chassis.contribution: Bioprinted human PDL/alveolar-bone microtissue with cohesion, viability, and shape retention under microfluidic flow.
published_chassis.transfer_limit: No root-facing cementum interface, inserted ligament fibers, or tooth-scale function.

published_chassis.contribution: Oriented fiber guidance in a rat periodontal fenestration-defect model.
published_chassis.transfer_limit: Open defect model and short follow-up; not retained-tooth impact repair.

model_components: Root-facing dentin/cementum-relevant mineral surface, with surface identity explicitly recorded
A non-mineralized ligament compartment containing donor-tracked PDL fibroblasts or PDL progenitor cells
A separate bone-facing compartment containing donor-tracked osteogenic cells
Spatially guided collagen bundles tested for insertion into both mineralized boundaries
Perfused endothelial support and cyclic mechanical loading introduced only after static two-interface acceptance

stages.name: Root-facing benchmark
stages.decision: Reproducible viability, migration, surface continuity, and orientation; no cementogenesis claim.

stages.name: Two-compartment interface
stages.design_reference: 2022 human PDL-bone microtissue plus root-facing benchmark
stages.decision: Compare homogeneous and biphasic architectures; reject mineral bridging.

stages.name: Fiber insertion
stages.decision: Require continuous bundles inserted at both interfaces, not just aligned cells or surface coverage.

stages.name: Transport and mechanics
stages.design_reference: Add perfusion, then calibrated cyclic loading
stages.decision: Require viable depth, recoverable compliance, and no interface loss or bone bridge.

stages.name: Orthotopic transfer
stages.decision: Assess tooth position, pulp, gingiva, resorption, function, and stability after temporary support withdrawal.

threshold_policy: Freeze numeric thresholds only after assay repeatability and matched healthy-reference distributions are available. Do not invent a universal PDL stiffness, fiber-angle, or ligament-width cutoff.
analysis_policy: Retain donor and batch as biological units; do not treat sections or fields as independent replicates.
Blind architecture labels for histology and mechanics scoring where feasible.
Compare mechanics only under matched sample geometry, fixture, and loading history.
Report viability, PDL identity, osteogenic drift, inflammation, interface insertion, mineral bridging, and mechanics as separate outcomes.
A construct that is stiff because of mineral bridging fails regardless of bulk load capacity.
limitations: No wet-lab work or treatment has been performed in this repository.
In-vitro repair cannot show correction of a displaced tooth or lifelong stability.
No numeric acceptance thresholds are available until a calibrated assay and matched reference distributions exist.
Human PDL chronological-age references remain sparse; cell source age, root maturity, disease state, and tooth type must be recorded rather than collapsed into a single youth score.
